From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivCP IAM playbook & SSO integration: workshop notes

Team / Acme ops,

Thanks again for the workshop this morning — great alignment on goals. I drafted a concise playbook (attached) that captures the proposed control-plane identity pattern for Private CP:

- SSO: SAML IdP (Okta) primary for admin console access; IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows supported.
- SCIM: group-sync from Okta mapped to Redwood roles (Admin, Operator, Readonly).
- IAM roles: short-lived RBAC tied to SCIM groups; service accounts issued via internal CA for automation.
- Audit: KMS-wrapped keys and audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM per the retention SLA.

Open questions I flagged in the doc: group-to-role mapping edge cases, delegated role escalation process, and network segmentation during cutover. Please review the attached and add any missing blockers.

Attachments: privcp_playbook_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Proposed next steps:
1) Dev: finalize SCIM group mapping template (by EOD 9/15)
2) Olga: validate network egress rules for IdP/SCIM endpoints (by 9/16)
3) Laura: coordinate customer test window and sign-off criteria (by 9/17)

I'll consolidate responses and share an updated playbook.

– Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-15T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivCP IAM playbook & SSO integration: workshop notes

Markus — thanks, good starter doc. A few quick notes inline and a CSV with the SCIM -> role mapping template attached.

- SCIM group naming: recommend prefixing with "rw-" to avoid collisions with customer groups.
- Mapping: prefer explicit deny rules for high-priv groups rather than relying on absence of grant.
- Token lifetime: propose 15m for short-lived management tokens, refreshable via OIDC exchange for automation.

Attachment: scim_group_mapping.csv (CSV, 4KB)

Question for Olga: SCIM provisioning will originate from Okta IP ranges; do we need special NAT rules or can the control plane accept connections via the existing egress NAT? If NAT constraints exist, we should add a stub in the playbook for a proxy.

Thanks — quick network check:

- Okta SCIM endpoint outbound: okta.com IP ranges are dynamic; we advise customers to allow egress to okta.com on 443 and use DNS allowlist rather than fixed IPs.
- If customer requires fixed egress IPs, we need to broker via a proxy in their VPC (see network-checklist.xlsx attached).
- TLS termination: control plane accepts TLS (client cert optional). If customer needs mTLS to Okta, we should document a proxy pattern.

I attached a brief network checklist for the customer testing window. If Acme's CloudOps insists on IP whitelisting, we'll need to schedule a short window to validate NAT behavior.

Attachment: network-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)
